title: Orchestrate INT8 weight-only calibration pipeline and regression smoke suite
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated orchestration layer and CI smoke-suite for INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ and AWQ variants) that validates calibration outputs, enforces accuracy gates, and produces per-model profile artifacts that are safe to use in production.

Scope:
- Add a calibration orchestration job that runs profile generation for new and updated models (FP32 -> INT8 weight-only) across our canonical calibration datasets.
- Produce standardized profile artifacts with metadata (model hash, calibration seed, layer-wise stats, quant params) stored in the profile registry.
- Implement a daily/nightly regression smoke-suite that evaluates quantized models on a small but representative prompt set (golden prompts + downstream task metrics).
- CI gating: enforce numeric accuracy regressions (per-metric delta thresholds) and flag profiles that exceed tolerances.
- Provide dashboards and alerting for profile quality drift, and a manual canary flow for safe rollout to Dedicated and Hosted pools.

Acceptance criteria:
- Orchestration job (k8s CronJob) can create and upload profile artifacts to registry for at least 6 model families.
- Regression smoke-suite runs in <45m on the debug cluster and emits a pass/fail verdict according to defined tolerances.
- CI presubmit job rejects PRs that introduce profiles that fail the smoke-suite.
- Dashboards show per-profile accuracy delta, token-level timing, and calibration coverage.
- Documentation and runbook (run/rollback) are published, with clear steps for manual canary.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full longform nightly evaluations, FP8 profiling, and end-to-end canary automation across Dedicated customers (follow-ups scheduled).
comments: 2026-03-06: Kickoff sync held with Applied ML (Aisha Patel), Runtime (Daniel Kim), and CI infra (Liam O'Connor). Agreed scope and initial calibration datasets: llama-family baselines + instruction-tuning subset.

2026-03-07: Prototype calibration runner PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3912. Basic GPTQ flow completes locally for a 7B model and emits JSON metadata. Performance note: single-model run ~28m on a V100-equivalent dev node.

2026-03-08: Decision: run both GPTQ and AWQ variants in parallel for each profile, store both artifacts. Rationale: short-term compatibility and comparison; long-term prefer AWQ when size/latency tradeoffs are demonstrated.

2026-03-09: Design review feedback from PM (Hannah Lee): require a per-model acceptance test that includes both a semantic similarity metric and the platform's conversational QA check. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10: Implemented deterministic seed control and layer sampling to reduce calibration nondeterminism. Benchmarked repeatability: profile metric variance reduced from 1.8% -> 0.3% across runs.
2026-03-11: CI infra: added 'quant-profile-smoke' job to the debug runner. Initial runs occasionally exceed 45m; next step to parallelize per-layer calibration and reduce CPU bottleneck.

2026-03-12: UX/observability request: include per-profile diff artifacts (golden vs candidate) and an automated gist link for failed runs. PR 3929 adds artifact upload to S3 bucket 'quant-profiles-staging'.
notes: Tradeoffs discussed: full-profile CI vs. smoke-suite. Chose smoke-suite to keep CI latency modest while catching common regressions.

Tolerance policy (temporary): per-task F1/EM delta <= 1.0% absolute or model flagged. For conversational QA composite score delta <= 0.8 points. These numeric thresholds will be tuned after two weeks of nightly runs.
Next steps: parallelize calibration (ENG-20137 spike), expand golden prompt set to include few-shot instruction prompts, add automated rollback hook for canary failures.
If a profile fails consistency checks but passes accuracy, mark as 'experimental' and keep out of default routing until manual review.
